newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX drops 1.9 pct, hit by Wall Street fall.
newsitem.headline: German DAX drops 1.9 pct, hit by Wall Street fall.

text.p: German shares dropped on Wednesday, unsettled by a loss of over one percent on Wall Street on Tuesday and disconcerted by the approaching possibility of a German interest rate rise.

The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session down 84.61 points, or 1.9 percent, at 4,278.48. September DAX futures were down even further, off 111 at 4,277. Twenty nine of the 30 blue chip stocks fell.
"People are certainly cautious today," said a dealer at a top Frankfurt bank.
"But the market needed a breather and that's what it is getting. We're not expecting this to go on."
Dealers said the market was on hold until U.S. July retail sales and wholesale prices are released this afternoon, fearing that unfavourable numbers there could steepen Wall Street's decline.

A secondary factor adding to the market's more negative mood were comments from the Bundesbank published this morning which showed the central bank was observing inflation trends closely and would act when necessary.

Dealers said these had been noted by the market but were having no real influence. Financial markets are now broadly of the view that it is only a matter of time before the Bundesbank starts to tighten the monetary policy screws.
Among shares in the news, Hoechst suffered losses in line with the broader market, falling 1.50 marks to 81 marks after the chemical company warned that its 1997 profit would be below 1996 levels.
Other news had minimal impact on share prices.
Deutsche Bank fell 2.20 marks to 117.50 after dismissing as "pure speculation" a press report that suggested it was keen to buy AGF, a French insurer.
